Unknown planet, Village

Since he had agreed to taking Jhoka in, albeit reluctantly, he was going to do it on his terms. Despite the lost worlds, the lost war, and really the lost people he still was fighting a never-ending insurgency against an enemy that was assumed to be long since defeated. Amukkan was gone, missing, and his so-called Golden Fleet had been whittled down to a handle of capital ships and assorted picket vessels that fled into unknown space.

That wasn't the goal though, they weren't eradicated like he had promised; like they all had promised centuries ago.

They were still out there, still a threat, so he was still an old sailor waging his war and he needed crew and not servants to do it.

"Teekus, chief wants to know why you call us here," Inzili whispered, glancing around at the growing crowd. "She is unhappy already with this business."

Who the fuck cares what that fat fuck's happy about. She could worry about stepping on scaly toes all she wanted, he didn't give a shit since they would be gone in a few days anyway. Maybe they would come back at some point, he didn't exactly mind them that much, but he had his fill of horny amazon lizards and their obsession with licking hands. They were kinda dicks to the girl in front of him anyway; her big, amber eyes told him she was more nervous of the people behind her than the alien in front.

Yeah, he knew her type. With his cold, blue eyes he peered into her, maybe right into her soul, and found what he suspected was there all along.

"Babe, translate for me. Tell her to straighten the fuck up."

Almost jumping at his words, Inzili glanced over at him quickly and said to Jhoka, "he says to stand up tall, I will translate."

"Yes, Zuua," she mumbled, steadying her posture and puffing out her chest to look as big and tall as he did.

"No talking."

Jhoka nodded quickly, furrowing her brow as she glared ahead.

Matching Stan's raised voice, Inzili cleared her throat and declared, "who here gives this girl away?"

"I do," the chief answered, folding her arms across her chest, "I give this girl away."

"Is she fit, healthy..." she paused to think of the right word, "and has a good mind?"

"Good enough."

All Inzili could do was nod to her male, obviously the impromptu ceremony had to go on despite the displeasure of the village chief. Stan turned to her and stared with a cold expression, his robotic movements were so out of the ordinary that she almost forgot to hand him the tiny pins he had given her. They were some type of hard, black-colored plastic shaped like rectangles with a single diagonal stripe running through them painted silver; she had always wondered why he carried them.

With smooth motion he took them in hand and clutched them in his left fist before addressing her directly, Inzili still translating.

"Jhoka of the Nine Lodge Clan, able, healthy, and sound of mind," he allowed the words to linger for a moment, "repeat after me."

Inzili huffed in frustration as she gave him a stern look that he ignored.

"I, your name, pledge to faithfully support and defend the Federal Republic of Seylonis in accordance with the Constitutional Articles against all enemies, foreign and domestic," he paused and resisted the urge to grin when she absolutely butchered the untranslatable words, "that I will bear allegiance to the same; and that I will obey the lawful orders of the Chancellor of the Federal Republic of Seylonis, and the lawful orders of the officers appointed over me..."

He let the words translate and sink in, Inzili having figured out to follow his cadence and let Jhoka's quivering voice have a chance to repeat each line by itself. Everyone in the crowd was still, even the chief had lost her annoyed expression, and he waited until a tense silence gripped everyone before continuing.

"... In accordance with the Uniform Code of Military Justice. So help me God."

She finished and hesitated slightly at the last part, Inzili obviously translated it in different terms for Jhoka but evoking their diety was obviously quite serious. That hesitation didn't last, the girl steeled herself and finished strong, her back straight and firm as she stood before him ready for anything.

"Sailor recruit, repeat after me," he began, steadying himself and looking at his companion. "Let her say the rest as I do. No translations."

"He tells you to repeat after him, to take the oath in his tongue," she whispered, shuffling out of the way.

Jhoka steadied herself further with a stern expression, she was obviously taking this quite serious. He didn't expect that she'd be able to keep up in the next part, though because it couldn't be translated, it had to happen as it happened for him and so many of his brothers and sisters in arms. Sometimes there would be some backwoods yokel from Tegantu or Voprux who couldn't speak a lick of English, but they still recited the words. Somehow it made it more special when they learned what oath they took later on, when they figured out the common language enough to understand it. Just like them those words would mean something to her, and not just because she was some clumsy, half-savage tribal either... No, this was something that had real magic to it.

He reached in his vest pocket and clicked a button on the portable computer, passing it off to his lover.

"I have chosen to become a Federation Sailor."

Without Inzili's help Jhoka could only blink before she stumbled through the alien words, her voice still shaky and unsure. He remembered to go slow and without the thick drawl.

"I will be loyal to my country," his voice gained a small amount of volume, "the Constitution, and it's laws."

An electric sensation started to flow up his back and, evidently, the same effect was on her as her body fought off an excited shudder as she spoke.

"I will be loyal to my shipmates."

That line came back clear and with conviction. Good.

"I will be honest and act with dignity at all times," he paused, "and I will encourage my shipmates to do the same."

Those pins in his hand felt like they had gained some weight, they were more than the plastic and steel they were made of.

"I will be a professional and wear the uniform with pride, accepting the consequences of my actions."

Almost done.

"I will be committed to excellence, honor, and courage."

As soon as she finished those words his body tensed, with a quick motion he backhanded her as hard as he could with his left fist.

"I will bear no more blows to my honor, my integrity, nor my person," he barely paused to let her catch up, her eyes glowing with hot anger as she recited the words, "I will defend the innocent, I will come to the aid of the oppressed, and I will not quit even as I take my last breath."

As she finished the words he stuck the collar pins through her woven tunic and gave her a hard, firm salute; he almost smiled when she mimicked him.

"I am a Federation Sailor."

Her bloody lip curled into a smirk as she recited the words. He recognized that look, she might not have understood them individually but he knew that she understood she belonged now. Belonging was worth more than hollow promises, a good crew was a family of sorts, a single unit greater than the sum of it's parts.

When he took that same oath and recited the creed it was after he had lost everything, it made him feel a sense of purpose and belonging. Sometimes outsiders looked at it and called it brainwashing and cultish, maybe it was, but for a kid like him it probably saved him from going off the deep end all those years ago. When he left ships behind as an enlisted man it put him shoulder to shoulder with marines, who took their own oath, and they seemed to draw in all the broken and troubled kids. A marine serving the federation was a mean motherfucker, gave as good as they got and then some, but in the end they served with honor. Those words, the blood on her teeth, the needles in his spine made him remember those men and women and his own sacred oath.

That sense of belonging he had wasn't some stupid platitude either, it came after surviving the attack on his world and then the grueling accelerated boot camp. Maybe she was a bit worse off though, they both took the oath as orphans but at least he didn't have to suffer the pain of being discarded.

Dropping the salute he stepped back with methodical precision. "Recruit, mount up, we leave in five."

"He say to go wait in the... thing we came in, we're leaving soon," Inzili translated before switching to his language, "why you do this?"

"Honestly I'm about fuckin' done with these people," he muttered with a disapproving scowl, "buncha fuckin' jackasses, might as well send her off all special like. She'll never forget this, but just in case I knocked her shit silly that recordin' will help keep it fresh for her."

Had they been alone she might have pounced on him right there, he was such a sweetheart when he wanted to be! "Teekus, you not regret this. I promise."

"You bet your sweet ass I won't."

That sounded ominous enough for her to feel a rush of concern, but she didn't lose her bright smile as he walked off.
